reason: Lower pressure should let dissolved volatiles escape, advancing the steam-rich atmosphere goal.
expectation: Rising melt will release gases, possibly including water vapor; I’m unsure whether that alone forms the atmosphere.

alternatives.reason: Convection may help the surface cool, but I’ll follow the water-release process first.

effect: The bubbles show that falling pressure releases existing volatiles; I’ll turn to the remaining surface process.
reaction: The distinction between releasing hydrogen and creating it is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may bring heat and melt toward the surface.
expectation: Convection will move hot material within Earth, perhaps toward the surface; I’m unsure what it will create.

effect: Upwelling links interior convection to the surface, providing a route for both outgassing and cooling.
reaction: The connection between buoyancy and surface activity is clear.
reason: Combining the bubbles with upwelling rock seems likely to release the gases at the surface.
expectation: The rising rock may carry exsolved gases into the atmosphere, though further steps could be needed.

alternatives.reason: Cooling the upwelling rock could advance the solid-surface goal, but I want to follow the gas first.

effect: The gases have reached the surface as volcanic plumes; gravity may now retain them around Earth.
reaction: The reminder that volcanic gas is not breathable air is useful.
reason: Gravity may gather the released gases into an atmosphere, advancing the first goal.
expectation: Some volcanic gas will be retained around Earth, possibly forming a steam-rich atmosphere.

alternatives.reason: Cooling upwelling rock could advance the surface goal, but I want to finish the outgassing path first.

effect: The released gases formed a steam-rich atmosphere, completing the first goal; the solid surface remains.
reaction: It is useful to see that Earth retains only part of the released gas.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may cool the upwelling rock.
expectation: Heat will escape to space, allowing some surface rock to cool or solidify.

effect: The surface has begun solidifying while hot rock remains mobile underneath; further cooling may establish the solid surface.
reaction: The contrast between a solid skin and a moving interior is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly continues cooling the lava skin.
expectation: The skin will cool further into a more solid surface, though it may remain unstable.

effect: Cooling produced a young basaltic crust; the remaining step may connect it to the moving interior.
reaction: The local nature of the solidification is a useful qualification.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly addresses the goal of a solid surface above moving rock.
expectation: The crust will remain above convecting hot rock, though it may be reworked.

effect: Convection fractures and reworks the crust, creating future routes for water; the surface goal is not yet complete.
reaction: The link between volcanic fractures and later water movement is intriguing.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may establish the crust above upwelling rock.
expectation: The upwelling rock will interact with the cracked crust, perhaps producing a continually renewed surface.

effect: Upwelling and cracked crust produced a volcanic surface with solid ground, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The coexistence of lava and solid ground makes the result tangible without suggesting the planet is hospitable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following dissolved volatiles from pressure-driven bubbles to a retained steam atmosphere was worthwhile: it explained outgassing without implying that it creates hydrogen.

leastWorthwhile.text: The successive crust-cooling steps felt somewhat repetitive, especially when each offered only one combination.

surprise.text: The cracked crust creating possible routes for later water was an intriguing connection between interior activity and the next stage.

arbitrary.text: The final combination of cracked crust with upwelling rock had a clear general purpose, but why it was a separate step after convection fractured the crust was less clear.

continue.text: Yes. The prospect of seeing water move through the newly fractured crust makes the next stage appealing, although the forced sequence was less engaging than the explanations.
